title: How it was tested
intro: Every number on this page is computed from the result files committed in evaluation/results.

blocks.title: What was tested, and what was not
blocks.text: Collision verdicts are tested on a simulator whose ground truth CARAI never sees: 3D vehicles, true markings that differ from the assumed standard, camera roll, yaw and noise. Seeds for the dev, test and shift splits were fixed in advance; the code was developed on dev only, frozen, and then run once on test and shift. Each layer is tested separately: the reasoning layer with true tracks, then the full pipeline from pixels.

callout.text: No real collision footage with ground truth was available to us under a licence that permits this use, so the collision verdicts are validated on simulation only. Real footage was used for the dashcam speed mode (see the Real dashcam footage tab).

blocks.text: The frozen run showed that every harmful end-to-end error on test happened 70-130 m from the camera, where one image row spans 0.65-2.5 m of road. v2.1 adds two rules derived from the stated priors, not fitted: neither contact nor 'no contact' is claimed when one image row at the vehicles spans more road than twice the vehicle-length uncertainty (0.7 m); and 'no contact' must also hold if a hidden lead braked at the envelope's 8 m/s^2 (or a hidden follower did not brake). It also fixes a crash on an empty Monte Carlo set. Because test motivated these rules, v2.1 is scored on test2, a split defined and committed before v2.1 was run on it (same distribution as test).

blocks.text: For 'prior mismatch' scenes the true markings differ from the assumed standard. v2's error there is measured against the error the wrong prior implies (it cannot be identified from one view); v1's is raw. The duty-cycle check flagged 1 of 1 accepted scenes whose dash proportions differ from the standard.

blocks.text: Each fault is injected into otherwise clean clips (two vehicles, no collision) analysed by the unchanged pipeline (v2.1). 'Speed error' is the worst error among the speeds CARAI reports, so it includes tracking errors: on the clean clips, every dispute was raised on a reconstruction that really was 20-40 % wrong (a tracking failure), and two tracking errors (16 % and 34 %) went unflagged. The last two rows are faults no check can see from a single static camera; they are listed so the blind spots are explicit.
